hook: SCP-2094 is a performer from Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting who can stretch his mouth to absurd lengths and store anything inside himself, a working car included. The early interviews are loud, crude and very funny, and that is deliberate: hold on to how he sounds in them. Later parts of the article deal with self-harm, a suicide attempt and children being taken from their homes.
whyItMatters: It's a strong character piece for the Circus of the Disquieting, letting one of its performers defend it instead of showing it only from the Foundation's side. The article is tagged both comedy and bittersweet, and its structure earns both: the voice that carries the first half is exactly what the second half takes away and then slowly gives back. Dr. Anniston's reports also show the caretaking side of the Foundation, with treatment plans, budgets and real fondness sitting in the same letters.
thingsToNotice: Early details pay off later: the trunk marked for "Essie", his silence when asked why he was left in it, and his loyalty to Manny, the man with the upside-down face who led him away from his mother's house as a child. In the December incident he wakes begging Manny not to take anything, then loses his memories of the circus and sinks into depression, at one point trying to swallow himself. Years later he recovers, and in the final interview explains the trunk: Manny had begun bringing in children who were taken rather than rescued, and when a girl who could fall apart and reassemble herself cried to go home, he hid her in his mouth and returned her. Manny struck him, then locked him in the trunk in front of everyone for the Foundation to find, and he still allows that Manny at least sent him somewhere safe.
